cards.text: Last time, Pharaoh ordered that every son born to the Hebrews be thrown into the Nile. Now a man from the house of Levi marries a Levite woman. Friend, that is a BRAVE time to say “I do.”

cards.question: With Pharaoh's order hanging over every Hebrew home, the Levite woman conceives. What does she give birth to?

cards.text: When she sees he's a beautiful child, she hides him. Hiding a BABY, friend? I can't even hide a chocolate chip from MYSELF.

cards.question: The Levite mother manages to keep her baby boy hidden for three months.

cards.text: Then the day comes when she can no longer hide him. So this mama gets to work.

cards.question: The mother can't hide her son anymore. What does she get for him?

cards.text: She coats the basket with tar and pitch, then places her son inside. Tar AND pitch. This woman is not playing around with leaks.

cards.question: The mother sets the basket with her baby among the ___ along the bank of the Nile.

cards.text: So the basket sits in the reeds, and now comes the waiting. I know waiting, friend. Years in a junk drawer made me a PROFESSIONAL.

cards.question: Someone from the baby's family stands at a distance by the Nile. Who is it?
Why does the baby's sister stand at a distance from the basket?

answers.text: To see what would happen to him
To wait for their mother to return
To keep strangers away from the reeds

cards.text: Soon the daughter of Pharaoh comes down to bathe in the Nile, with her attendants walking along the riverbank. Of ALL the people in Egypt, it's Pharaoh's DAUGHTER.

cards.question: Pharaoh's daughter spots the basket among the reeds and leaves it right where it is.

cards.text: She sends her maidservant to bring the basket to her. She opens it, and there's the little boy, crying.

cards.question: Pharaoh's daughter opens the basket and finds a little boy crying. What does she feel for him?
Pharaoh's daughter looks at the baby in the basket and says, “This is one of the ___ children.”

cards.text: Then the baby's sister walks right up to Pharaoh's daughter. Friend, I used to get nervous when the drawer just OPENED.

cards.question: The baby's sister speaks up to Pharaoh's daughter. What does she offer to do?

answers.text: Call a Hebrew woman to nurse him
Carry the basket up to the palace
Watch the baby while she bathes

cards.text: “Go ahead,” Pharaoh's daughter tells her. And off the girl goes.

cards.question: The sister goes to find a Hebrew woman to nurse the baby. Who does she call?

cards.text: Pharaoh's daughter turns to the woman and says, “Take this child and nurse him for me.” And she isn't done talking.

cards.question: Pharaoh's daughter promises to pay the boy's mother wages to nurse him.

cards.text: So the mother takes her own son and nurses him, and she gets PAID for it. Three months of hiding this baby, and now he's on the ROYAL payroll.
When the child has grown older, his mother brings him to Pharaoh's daughter.

cards.question: The boy's mother brings him to Pharaoh's daughter. What happens to him?

answers.text: He returns to the house of Levi

cards.question: Pharaoh's daughter names the boy Moses and explains, “I drew him out of the ___.”

cards.text: Moses, the boy drawn out of the Nile, is now the son of Pharaoh's daughter. Hang onto this one, friend, because his story is just getting started.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 5 quotes "This is one of the ___ children.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card states a fact from Exodus 1:22 (Pharaoh's order to throw every Hebrew son into the Nile), but it cites only Exodus 2:1. That fact has no reference.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The joke says the Levite couple married during Pharaoh's decree. The text doesn't say when they married relative to the order. Exodus 7:7 shows Aaron was three years older than Moses, which suggests they married before the decree.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. It repeats the answer to card 8 (the basket sits in the reeds) and adds only a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The question says the person is "someone from the baby's family." That rules out the wrong answer "The midwife Shiphrah."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke compares two different actions. The sister boldly speaks up to Pharaoh's daughter, but the comparison is about being nervous when a drawer opens. The actions don't match, so the joke doesn't click instantly.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The question tells the baker the sister is finding "a Hebrew woman." That rules out the wrong answer "A servant from the palace."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke says the baby is "on the ROYAL payroll." In Exodus 2:9 the wages go to the mother, not the child, so the joke blurs who gets paid.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it.

findings.problem: The last story card opens by recapping what cards 14 and 15 already answered (Moses is now the son of Pharaoh's daughter, drawn from the water). The last verse was already asked on a choice card, so this card should be only the story-isn't-over line.
